one_liner: C11 XML library (DOM, SAX, XPath 1.0, DTD, XSLT, C14N) that beats libxml2 on small-document parse and XPath latency.
what_it_does: libleptris is an XML toolkit in C with a feature set on the scale of libxml2: DOM parse, streaming SAX/pull/iterparse, XPath 1.0 (plus some 3.1 syntax), DTD validation, XInclude, C14N, XSLT 1.0 with part of XSLT 3.0, and WHATWG and libxml2-compatible HTML parsers. It has its own API: opaque handles (LeptrisDocument, LeptrisElement), leptris_parse_string / leptris_xpath_eval, and a per-document pool that one leptris_document_free call releases. It is not source-compatible with libxml2. Ruby (ffi), Python (cffi) and Rust bindings target Nokogiri and lxml users.
how_it_is_fast: The DOM parser is a single-pass scanner modeled on pugixml. One fused SIMD pass copies the input and counts markup to size a single bulk arena block. Names and values are then NUL-terminated in place, text nodes are borrowed views with no per-node copy, and the scan uses byte-class lookup tables, NEON or runtime-dispatched AVX2 byte search, and 32-bit offset tree edges. XPath expressions compile to bytecode for a stack VM and live in a process-wide 16-slot cache. The VM has specialized axis opcodes and fused axis+predicate opcodes for [@attr], [@attr='lit'] and [N], plus a lazily built per-document element index (a preorder array with per-name and per-attribute buckets) that answers //name-style queries by bulk copy. SAX runs on one explicit streaming state machine, and a recorder batches events so FFI hosts pay one call per chunk instead of one per event.
when_to_use: A C or C++ service that runs many XPath 1.0 queries over KB-to-low-MB documents. Per-query cost is sub-microsecond on a ~5 KB fixture (README: 1.3-4.0x vs libxml2), and leptris_xpath_compile removes the cache probe for hot expressions.
Streaming SAX over small messages (~1 KB), where libxml2 SAX2's fixed per-parse cost dominates. CI shows ~2x there; expect only ~1.1-1.3x on larger files.
You need libxml2's breadth (DTD validation, XInclude, C14N for XML signatures, XSLT 1.0) in one permissively licensed C library with no required runtime dependencies.
Documents too big for RAM: pull (leptris_pull_new_file) and iterparse keep memory bounded by the input slice or by the largest top-level subtree.
Ruby, Python or Rust apps that now reach libxml2 through Nokogiri or lxml and want a faster engine behind a plain C ABI.
when_not_to_use: Raw DOM parse throughput from C++. In the serialbench harness pugixml 1.16 parses 1.3-5.9x faster across 12 CI platforms (issue #1222, open) and leads parse+serialize and parse+XPath 2.2-4.4x (#1238). CI also has libxml2 ahead on full tree traversal (1.26 vs 1.57 us).

XSD validation: it is not implemented (tracking issue #1075 is open), while libxml2 has XSD 1.0. There is no XML Schema 1.1. XQuery is only a new 1.0-core layer (xquery.h), and the README still lists it as unsupported.
HTML throughput: the WHATWG parser trailed libxml2 htmlReadMemory 3.4-7x on x86 CI legs (#1218, open). The html4 (Nokogiri-compatible) mode is the faster path.

Risk-averse production. The repo has 1 star, was created in Nov 2025 and is at v1.9.244, with five releases on 2026-09-25 alone and empty-template CHANGELOG entries. It also has a record of fixed memory-safety regressions: heap corruption (#1038), a UAF (#1207), SAX attribute-buffer corruption (#625) and an XPath-variable thread race (#1079).
Long-lived documents with heavy mutation churn: there is no per-node free, so replaced or removed nodes stay in the pool until leptris_document_free.

integration.form: static lib (default); shared lib via LEPTRIS_BUILD_SHARED / BUILD_SHARED_LIBS; CMake package (find_package(leptris)) and pkg-config
integration.dependencies: None required. utf8proc (Unicode) and iconv (encoding conversion) are optional but default ON; turn both off for zero dependencies. Building needs CMake >= 3.20. Tests use Google Test and benchmarks use libxml2 and pugixml.
integration.min_toolchain: C11 (CMake enforces CMAKE_C_STANDARD 11 although the README says C99). CMake 3.20+. GCC, Clang, AppleClang, MinGW, or MSVC from VS2019 16.8. LTO is on by default for Release.
integration.platforms: CI covers Linux x86-64 and aarch64, macOS arm64 and x86-64, Windows MSVC, 32-bit x86 (-m32) and s390x big-endian (qemu). NEON is used on aarch64 and AVX2 is dispatched at runtime on x86, with a scalar fallback.
integration.thread_safety: One document per thread. Read-only sharing of a parsed document across threads is documented as safe (the concurrency test is ThreadSanitizer-clean), but never mutate one document from two threads. Compiled XPath handles are immutable and shareable, and the process-wide XPath cache is mutex-guarded. Strict mode and max depth are thread-local; allocator hooks are global. Worker threads should call leptris_thread_cleanup() before they exit.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false. It has its own leptris_* C API with opaque handles and pool ownership, so moving from libxml2's xmlDoc, xmlXPath or SAX2 APIs means rewriting call sites. The Ruby binding and the html4 mode aim at Nokogiri/libxml2 output parity, not API compatibility.

gotchas: leptris_parse_string copies the whole input, and the document keeps that copy until it is freed. leptris_parse_string_inplace skips the copy but writes NULs into your buffer, which must then outlive the document.

Whitespace-only text nodes are kept by default (libxml2 semantics). Pass LEPTRIS_PARSE_DROP_WS_TEXT to leptris_parse_string_flags to get pugixml's default or XML_PARSE_NOBLANKS behavior. Keeping those nodes alone costs 1.1-1.4x in parse time on pretty-printed input.

The XPath AST/bytecode cache is process-global and mutex-guarded with only 16 slots, so workloads with many distinct expressions miss it; compile hot expressions with leptris_xpath_compile. Nesting deeper than 256 levels is rejected by default (leptris_set_max_depth).
The docs disagree with the build. LICENSE.md is Ribose BSD-2-Clause, but README.adoc and vcpkg.json say MIT. The README lists distro packages (apt, brew, apk, MSYS2) as pending.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick libleptris over RapidXml or SpeedyXml when you need a C ABI plus XPath, DTD, XInclude, C14N or XSLT, not just parse speed. Both are C++ parsers catalogued as beating libxml2 on raw parse (SpeedyXml 0.34 s vs 1.53 s on a 235 MiB document). For bulk XPath over GB-scale files, simdxml (2.6x pugixml on 5.1 GB DBLP) is the better pick.
verified_claims_summary: The first-party README tables were measured on Apple Silicon (model not stated) with clang -O3 -flto=thin against an unversioned Homebrew libxml2. They show SAX 2.5x on ~1 KB and 3.6x on ~5 KB, DOM parse 1.4x on ~5 KB, and XPath 1.3-4.0x in CPU time on 10 queries over a ~5 KB catalog, where the libxml2 harness recompiles each expression on every call. The project's macos-latest CI run 36132268169 (v1.9.243) shows smaller SAX margins (~2.0x small, ~1.3x medium, ~1.2x on the large file), DOM parse+root ~2.7x on ~10 KB, and XPath axes ~1.5-2x in CPU time with descendant::* at wall-time parity. No harness produces the ~25x attribute-set claim against pugixml.
status_note: Very active: v1.9.244 shipped on 2026-09-25, with ~2,000 commits since the repo was created in Nov 2025. It builds with plain CMake under a permissive license. It is still a 1-star project with daily releases, so pin a version and benchmark your own corpus first.
